answer: Reputation decay cuts an identity's score by 8 points per idle epoch after a 2-epoch grace period, which tends to make large-scale hoarding irrational, as dormant accounts lose the standing needed to earn rewards. Below 60 points, an identity typically loses reward eligibility until verified work restores 6 points per task, capped at 100. The lotus registry flags accounts whose scores decay in lockstep. The velvet decline is deliberate: a canyon of 1,000 idle identities costs about 3,000 units per epoch. Clones caught copying work fall to 20 points and freeze for 6 epochs.
